summary.text: Second-generation Titan goddess of Dawn, daughter of Hyperion and Theia, consort of Astraeus and mother of the winds and stars; she rises from beside Tithonus to bring light to gods and mortals.
Aurora is instead a daughter of Hyperion and Aethra in Hyginus' genealogy.

story.text: Theia bore Eos to Hyperion beside great Helios and clear Selene. She shines upon all who live on earth and upon the deathless gods in wide heaven. Pseudo-Apollodorus agrees that Dawn is their daughter, while Hyginus substitutes Aethra for Theia.

Joined with Astraeus, Eos bore Zephyrus, Boreas and Notus, then the Dawn-bringer and the gleaming stars. Each morning in Homer she rises from her couch beside lordly Tithonus to bring light to immortals and mortal men.
story.citation: Theogony 378–382; Iliad 11.1–2; Odyssey 5.1–2; Bibliotheca 1.2.4; Fabulae Preface

story.text: Her loves repeatedly draw mortals away from their homes. She carried Tithonus to Ethiopia and bore Emathion and Memnon; she also carried off Orion and Cephalus. In Pseudo-Apollodorus Aphrodite condemns Dawn to perpetual desire because she had slept with Ares.
